name: C# and DotNET
scope: An individual with INTERMEDIATE proficiency in C# and .NET, with 3-6 years of experience, should have a solid grasp of advanced language features such as delegates, events, lambda expressions, LINQ (both query and method syntax), generics (including constraints), and asynchronous programming with async and await, understanding tasks, threads, and concurrency issues. They should be capable of developing web applications using ASP.NET MVC and ASP.NET Core, including Razor Pages and Blazor (both Server and WebAssembly), with knowledge of middleware, dependency injection, and configuration management. They should be adept at designing and implementing RESTful APIs using ASP.NET Web API or ASP.NET Core API, understanding routing, model binding, validation, authentication, and authorization mechanisms like JWT and OAuth. They should have experience building desktop applications using WPF (with MVVM pattern, data binding, commands, and resource dictionaries) or WinForms, and be comfortable with XAML. They should possess strong skills in database interactions using Entity Framework Core (Code First and Database First approaches, migrations, LINQ queries, eager vs. lazy loading) or ADO.NET, and be able to write complex SQL queries and stored procedures. They apply design patterns such as Singleton, Factory, Repository, Observer, and Dependency Injection, and adhere to SOLID principles and architectural patterns like MVC and MVVM to create maintainable and scalable applications. They are proficient in unit testing with frameworks like MSTest, NUnit, or xUnit, write testable code, use mocking libraries like Moq, understand code coverage, and may practice Test-Driven Development (TDD). They are skilled in using Git for version control, including branching strategies (GitFlow, feature branches), merging, rebasing, and resolving conflicts, and collaborate using platforms like GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket through pull requests and code reviews. They can debug and troubleshoot complex issues using Visual Studios debugging tools, performance profilers, and memory analyzers, optimize code for performance and resource management, and implement effective error handling and logging strategies using frameworks like NLog or log4net. They communicate technical concepts clearly, document code and APIs effectively, mentor junior developers, participate in architectural and design discussions, and contribute to improving coding standards and best practices. They have a basic understanding of CI/CD pipelines using tools like Azure DevOps, Jenkins, or GitHub Actions, can set up automated builds, tests, and deployments, and have experience deploying applications to cloud platforms like Microsoft Azure (App Services, Azure Functions, Azure SQL Database) or AWS, and are familiar with containerization using Docker and orchestration with Kubernetes. They stay updated with the latest developments in C# and .NET, such as new language features (e.g., records, pattern matching enhancements, nullable reference types), and are proactive in learning and incorporating new technologies and methodologies that enhance development efficiency and software quality.
